text: Great. So I'm here to talk about tokenization. What is it? Why does it matter? And what is its future? So tokenization or real world asset tokenization, as we are focused on in Ondo is the representation of ownership of some asset on a blockchain, ideally a public blockchain, where that asset is not natively on that chain. You know, tokenization is great because tokens are transferable 24, 7, globally accessible, programmable. They have a lot of features that we like. You know, we've seen the value and the appeal of those features in the success of Bitcoin and other digitally native assets. And there is a desire in the marketplace to apply some of these features to traditional assets, particularly traditional financial assets. Historically, the focus, particularly in 2018, 2019, 2020, has been on taking the assets from traditional finance that feel the most broken from a settlement perspective. So private loans, funds, you know, these assets that are illiquid, slow to settle, you know, syndicated loans take, you know, days to weeks to settle and representing them in token form to try to make them, you know, more liquid and quick to settle. There's been a lot of money invested in these attempts, but they've generally not led to a whole lot. At Ondo, the benefit of tokenization that we're focused on is access, and we define access very broadly. So it's not just the ability to hold assets, but also to use them in defi wherever you want, and more broadly to create financial products and services that can be accessed by anyone, anywhere, at any time. We've seen the benefit of this focus on accessibility through stablecoins. Stablecoins are of course, the tokenized real world asset that has by far the largest product market fit to date, you know, over $200 billion circulating on public blockchains, despite the fact that they pay holders no yields. And so at Ondo, we started our journey into tokenization by asking how can we make stablecoins even better? And the obvious answer is by paying holders the yield from the treasuries that back the stablecoins. So we call these products yieldcoins. And we launched the first of our yield coins in early 2023 OUSG. It's a permissioned institutional fund that holds short term treasuries and is transferable 24,7 and programmable, but only between institutions, qualified purchasers, specifically who are onboarded to osg. The market reaction to that was really positive. But people wanted something that was more globally accessible to retail investors and that function more like a stablecoin as a bearer quasi permissionless asset.
